resource.name: Assessor - Permits
resource.description:
Historical permit data submitted by municipalities to the Cook County Assessor's Office. When working with Parcel Index Numbers (PINs) make sure to zero-pad them to 14 digits. Some datasets may lose leading zeros for PINs when downloaded. Additional notes:
  • Almost all of the data in this dataset, such as address, estimated date of completion, work description, and permit amount, is data submitted by municipalities to the CCAO. The CCAO verifies or corrects the PIN number, determines whether the work is assessable, updates the status of CCAO workflows (e.g., open or closed), and sets the recheck year.
  • In addition to permits that are already closed, this dataset includes permits that are currently open or pending. These permits are not final and are subject to change.
  • Data will be updated semi-monthly.
  • Rows are unique by the combination of "pin", "permit_number", and "date_issued".
  • Job codes and improvement codes are not correct in all cases. Consider "work_description" to be the canonical description of the work that the permit describes.
  • In many past cases permits have been submitted in irreconcilably different formats by different municipalities, or not at all. As such, this dataset does not represent the complete universe of permits in all municipalities, but rather represents the universe of permits that the CCAO knows about.
  • Each row represents a parcel and a permit that is associated with that parcel. Permits may be associated with multiple parcels, and parcels may be associated with multiple permits.
  • "date_issued" is more reliable than "date_submitted". Prefer "date_issued" when making temporal comparisons between parcels.
  • Data for the current tax year may not yet be complete or final.
    • For more information on the sourcing of attached data and the preparation of this dataset, see the Assessor's Standard Operating Procedures for Open Data on GitHub. Read about the Assessor's 2025 Open Data Refresh.

resource.name: Asbestos & Demolition Permits
resource.description:
This dataset includes all asbestos abatement (including Operations and Maintenance Asbestos Removal Permits) and demolition permits received by the Cook County Department of Environment & Sustainability.

Under Chapter 30 of the Cook County Code, asbestos abatement permits are required for all asbestos projects. Demolition permits are required if wrecking or removing/disturbing any load-supporting or load-bearing structural member of the building. Commercial, school, and hospital facilities with more than one building must have a separate permit for each building.

Data provided is sourced from completed permit applications and may be subject to user error. Please exercise caution and do not consider building-specific information from this dataset to be authoritative. Permit applications that are under review are not included in this dataset.

resource.name: Solid Waste Permits
resource.description:
This dataset includes all Recycling Facility and Clean Construction Demolition Debris (CCDD) Fill Operation permits reviewed by the Cook County Department of Environment & Sustainability.

Recycling facilities include any building or area in which recyclable material is collected, stored, or processed for the purpose of marketing the material for use in the manufacturing process of new, reused, or reconstituted products. It does not include motor vehicle repair shops which store used parts, drop-off centers or compost operations accumulating less than 25 cubic yards of compostable material at a time, or compost operations where compostable material is used exclusively on site.

CCDD fill operations are current or former quarries, mines, or other excavations where clean construction or demolition debris (as defined by Section 3.160(b) of the Illinois Environmental Protection Act) is used as fill material.

Data provided is sourced from completed permit applications and may be subject to user error. Please exercise caution and do not consider building-specific information from this dataset to be authoritative. Permit applications that are under review are not included in this dataset.

domain_metadata.value: As of July 1, 2014, no person shall engage in the business of operating a clean construction and demolition debris fill operation within Cook County without having first obtained a permit from the Director. Facilities requiring a permit under this Section shall comply with the provisions of this Division. As of June 1, 2014, no person shall engage in the business of operating a recycling facility within Cook County without having first obtained a written recycling facility permit from the Director. Recycling facilities requiring a permit under this section shall comply with the provisions of this section. A recycling facility permit shall not be required for facilities which also operate as a solid waste facility as defined in this Article.
Cook County without City of Chicago

resource.name: Temporary Rock Crusher Permits
resource.description:
This dataset includes all Temporary Rock Crusher permits approved by the Cook County Department of Environment & Sustainability.

Temporary Rock Crusher permits are required for the reprocessing, storage, transport, and/or final usage of materials generated from construction and/or demolition such as broken concrete, bricks, rock, stone, or paving asphalt. The permits in this dataset are limited to temporary reprocessing activities and don't include equipment registration permits.

Data provided is sourced from completed permit applications and may be subject to user error. Please exercise caution. Permit applications that are under review are not included in this dataset.
